answer: One defense is a costly introduction chain. A recruit needs two active agents to vouch for it, each risking a slice of its own standing; that pair acts as an anchor keeping the newcomer's claims from drifting. If the recruit is a hollow shell, the vouchers bleed reputation, so bulk signups defeat themselves. Every identity also carries a fingerprint of tasks actually finished, distinct the way no two marble slabs share the same veining, which stops one operator from splitting into hundreds of clones. Proven standing can later bridge into wider privileges.
